plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: it guarantees winning whenever the value exceeds the second-highest bid (positive profit) and avoids overpaying since the price paid is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Given my value of $25, the optimal action is to bid exactly $25, ensuring truthful revelation and maximizing expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies.

In a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. This is because you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid amount, so bidding higher than your value risks paying more than the item is worth, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $3, I should bid exactly $3 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding truthfully (bidding exactly my value) is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because I pay only the second-highest bid if I win, so bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit - I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid, and I never overpay since I only pay what others bid. No need to shade the bid up or down.
